title: multipart serialization bottleneck causing tenant timeout surge and customer escalation runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers reported sustained 5xx and 504 timeouts after onboarding a feature that performs large multipart payloads (document ingestion). Initial signal shows correlation between high concurrent multipart requests from single tenants and spikes in backend latencies leading to downstream KV cache churn and proxy connection exhaustion. This ticket coordinates triage, short-term mitigations, and a longer-term fix (serialization + admission control).

Background: On 2025-02-17 evening we started seeing tenant-specific latency increases. Unlike previous retry storms, traces show requests queueing behind long-running multipart handlers at the edge proxy and the serving runtime. The runtime's KV cache compaction was triggered more aggressively due to uneven tokenization patterns for large documents, causing repeated cold-starts for attention KV slices for some infer requests. The combination produced 504s and client retries amplifying load.

Goal: Rapidly stabilize affected tenants and put a robust fix in place to prevent recurrence. Provide customer comms and postmortem artifacts.

Scope: Hosted API only (frontdoor proxy + runtime serving pool). Dedicated and Private customers may be impacted by analogous patterns; we will produce cross-team notes but not change Dedicated/Private infra in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Immediate mitigations deployed that reduce 5xx/504 rates for affected tenants by >90%
A short-term admission-control roll (per-tenant concurrent multipart cap) live and validated via synthetic load
Root cause analysis documented with timeline and evidence (traces, flamegraphs, KV cache metrics)
A proposed long-term design (serialization/streamed-handling + KV cache protectors) scoped and scheduled
Customer-facing status and follow-up (emails/Support replies) drafted and logged
updates: 2025-02-18 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Initial pager; correlated spike to tenant T-42 and large multipart ingestion. Created ticket and alerted SRE. Links: confluence/redwood/runtime-multipart-incident-2025-02 (WIP).

2025-02-18 10:05 - Lucas Moreno: Captured traces in X-Ray: root spans show 8–12s blocking inside proxy-layer body assembly for payloads >8MB. Added additional sampling and flamegraph dumps to /dashboards/ingest-multipart. PR created to enable extra tracing: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2378

2025-02-18 13:30 - SRE Team (K. Singh): Applied emergency temporary config on edge-proxy to limit concurrent upstream streams per connection from same tenant to 3. Observed initial drop in 504s for T-42. Noted increased 429 errors (expected) — added to customer comms.
mitigation_plan: - Edge-proxy: apply per-tenant concurrent-multipart cap (3) and shorten keepalive timeout to avoid connection pileup
- Gateway: enable immediate fast-fail for requests that would cause queueing beyond 5s at frontdoor; surface clear 429 with retry-after header
- Runtime: temporarily increase KV cache compaction threshold to avoid aggressive evictions while we stabilize
- Customer comms: notify affected tenants via shared Slack thread and support ticket with ETA and mitigation details
- Implement streaming ingestion path that avoids fully materializing multipart bodies in the proxy; hand-off to runtime as chunked stream
- Add admission controller for concurrent heavy ingestors per-tenant with configurable quotas in tenant profile
- Add KV-cache guard: protect hot KV shards from eviction during heavy single-tenant bursts (pinning heuristic)
- Rework connection serialization in frontdoor to use request multiplexing where safe; re-evaluate proxy connection reuse policies
- Integrate ingest workload classifier to route heavy document loads to specialized serving lanes (isolated pools)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tighter per-tenant caps reduce blast radius but may surface 429s to customers — tradeoff between graceful degrade and customer frustration
Increasing KV cache thresholds temporarily raises memory pressure; requires close watch on OOM metrics in runtime nodes
Streaming ingestion reduces peak memory and serialization time but requires runtime changes across languages and SDKs — longer rollout window
actions_taken: Edge-proxy configuration change deployed (hotfix) 2025-02-18 14:02 — per-tenant concurrent multipart cap set to 3; keepalive reduced from 90s to 20s. Rollout ID: rollout/edge-proxy/2025-02-18-14
Runtime compaction threshold bump deployed 2025-02-18 15:10 — observed KV eviction rate drop by 82% in affected pool
Synthetic replay test created 2025-02-19 by QA (script: ci/synthetic/multipart-replay.sh) — used to validate mitigation before broader rollout
Customer T-42 support update posted 2025-02-18 16:00 with mitigation summary and expected timeline for permanent fix (link to support ticket CT-8877)
next_steps: Finalize PR for edge-proxy metrics to expose per-tenant stream queue length (github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/2387) — Lucas to shepherd
Design review scheduled 2025-02-20 11:00 for streaming ingestion path (invite: runtime@redwood.com, sdk@redwood.com)
Estimate engineering work for admission controller and KV shard pinning — add to runtime backlog and assign owners
Prepare postmortem doc template and timeline: capture t0,t1,t2, mitigation windows and customer impact; publish in Confluence within 7 days
postmortem_notes: Preliminary root cause: combination of large multipart body assembly in proxy (blocking CPU/IO), per-tenant burst that pinned a subset of runtime KV shards, and client retries amplifying load.

Contributing factors: lack of per-tenant admission control for heavy ingesters; KV cache compaction tuned for average working set not bursty document ingestion patterns; long keepalive windows allowed connection pile-up.
Action items: implement admission controller + streaming ingestion (owner: Lucas), add KV guard rails (owner: S. Kim), adjust default keepalive and multiplexing policies (owner: Edge team)
